title: Omegle Alternatives in 2026: 9 Random Video Chat Sites Compared
description: An honest comparison of 9 Omegle alternatives: age rules, whether you need an account, what is free, and what each says about safety. Sources linked.
author: Naimish Omar
content:
Since Omegle closed in November 2023, a long list of sites has tried to replace it. This guide compares nine of them on the things that matter most: who they are for, whether you need an account, what is free, and what they say about safety.

**A note on fairness.** Vibelly is our product, so we have tried hard to describe every service using its own website, terms, and app store listings, plus reputable reporting. We only include facts we could source, and we say "not stated" when a service does not say. Everything was checked in October 2026, and these services change often, so check the linked sources before you decide.

If you want the criteria behind this comparison, read [How to Choose an Omegle Alternative](/blog/how-to-choose-an-omegle-alternative).

## Quick summary

| Service | Age rule | Account to chat | Platforms | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OmeTV | Adults, at your country's legal age | Not clearly stated | Web, iOS, Android | Free; paid VIP on Android |
| Chatroulette | 18+ | Not needed | Web, iOS, Android | Free |
| Emerald Chat | 18+, per its terms | Required | Web | Free; gender filter is Premium |
| Monkey | Not stated; Google Play rates it 12+ | Required (social login) | Android, web | In-app purchases |
| Chatrandom | Google Play rates it 18+ | Not stated | Web, Android, iOS | Free; in-app purchases |
| CamSurf | Google Play rates it 18+ | Not needed | Web, Android | Free; in-app purchases |
| Bazoocam | Not stated | Not stated | Web | Not stated |
| Uhmegle | Minors forbidden | Not needed | Web | Free |
| Vibelly | 18+, confirmed before every chat | Not needed | Web | Free; Premium from ₹49 a month |

Details and sources for every row are below.

## OmeTV

- **Age:** adults only, at the legal age in your country. Minors are banned even with parental consent.
- **Account:** the FAQ says signing in adds features like profiles and friends. Whether you can chat without one is not clearly stated.
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, and Android.
- **Cost:** video chat is free. The Android app has a paid "VIP Lounge" subscription. OmeTV's FAQ says there are no gender filters.
- **Safety:** a report button sends moderators a screenshot and the chat, moderators work 24/7, and users must show a real, uncovered face.
- **Worth knowing:** in October 2025, Australia's eSafety Commissioner said Apple and Google had removed the OmeTV app from their Australian app stores over child-grooming concerns. The website remained available.
- **Sources:** [OmeTV rules](https://ome.tv/rules/), [OmeTV FAQ](https://ome.tv/faq/), [eSafety Commissioner](https://www.esafety.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/eSafety-secures-removal-of-video-chat-service-used-for-child-grooming)

## Chatroulette

- **Age:** 18+, with an age confirmation before you start.
- **Account:** none needed.
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, and Android.
- **Cost:** free, including a country filter. Some extras use "Quids", a free in-app currency.
- **Safety:** describes AI and human moderation, automated video screening, and a 24/7 trust and safety team that reviews reports.
- **Worth knowing:** one of the originals, launched in November 2009. The same October 2025 LBC investigation that covered Uhmegle reported that Chatroulette did not require proof of age.
- **Sources:** [Chatroulette](https://chatroulette.com/), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatroulette), [LBC investigation](https://www.lbc.co.uk/news/exclusive/video-chatrooms-british-children/)

## Emerald Chat

- **Age:** 18+, per its terms of service.
- **Account:** required, using email, Google, or Facebook.
- **Platforms:** web. Its homepage mentions official phone apps but does not link a store listing.
- **Cost:** random text and video chat, interest matching, and group channels are free. The gender filter is labelled Premium.
- **Safety:** describes 24/7 human moderation, AI bot detection, and report and block tools.
- **Sources:** [Emerald Chat](https://emeraldchat.com/), [Terms of service](https://emeraldchat.com/terms-of-service/)

## Monkey

- **Age:** not stated on its website. Google Play rates the app 12+.
- **Account:** required, via social login.
- **Platforms:** Android app, plus a web version that its site directs iPhone and desktop users to.
- **Cost:** the app has in-app purchases and subscriptions. Prices are not stated.
- **Safety:** describes AI-powered moderation and a Safety Center.
- **Worth knowing:** with a 12+ rating on Google Play, Monkey is not an adults-only service, unlike most others on this list.
- **Sources:** [Monkey](https://www.monkey.app/), [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=cool.monkey.android)

## Chatrandom

- **Age:** Google Play rates the app 18+.
- **Account:** not stated.
- **Platforms:** web, Android, and iOS.
- **Cost:** free to download and video chat. The app has in-app purchases and advertises gender and location filters.
- **Safety:** not stated in the sources we could access.
- **Sources:** [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=chatrandom.com)

## CamSurf

- **Age:** Google Play rates the app 18+.
- **Account:** none needed. It says you can chat anonymously without signing up.
- **Platforms:** web and Android.
- **Cost:** free, with country and language filters. The app has in-app purchases.
- **Safety:** says it employs dozens of moderators, with reporting and temporary bans.
- **Sources:** [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=camsurf.com)

## Bazoocam

- **Age and account:** not stated on its homepage.
- **Platforms:** web.
- **Cost:** not stated.
- **Safety:** says it is moderated constantly by more than 40 people. Users must stay clothed or face a 20-day ban.
- **Worth knowing:** has built-in games you can play with the other person, like Tetris and tic-tac-toe.
- **Sources:** [Bazoocam](https://bazoocam.org/)

## Uhmegle

- **Age:** states that access by minors is strictly forbidden.
- **Account:** none needed, and no proof of age is required.
- **Platforms:** web.
- **Cost:** free.
- **Safety:** its landing page claims AI and human moderation.
- **Worth knowing:** launched shortly after Omegle closed. An LBC investigation published in October 2025 reported finding apparent under-18 users and sexual propositions on the site.
- **Sources:** [Uhmegle](https://uhmegle.com/), [LBC investigation](https://www.lbc.co.uk/news/exclusive/video-chatrooms-british-children/)

## Vibelly

- **Age:** 18+. You confirm you are 18 or older before every chat.
- **Account:** none needed to chat. Reporting someone requires signing in, so reports are tied to real accounts.
- **Platforms:** web, on phone and desktop browsers.
- **Cost:** random video chat (480p) and text chat are free. Vibelly Premium adds gender and country filters, 720p HD video, and voice-only calls, from ₹49 a month.
- **Safety:** every call has a Report button for signed-in users, reports are reviewed by hand, and signed-in accounts that break the rules are banned. Calls are encrypted in transit and never recorded. Vibelly does not use automated AI moderation.
- **Worth knowing:** Vibelly is newer and smaller than the long-running services above, so there may be fewer people online at quiet times.
- **Sources:** [Safety & Community Rules](/safety), [Pricing](/pricing)

## Which should you choose?

There is no single best option for everyone. If you want to start without an account, look at Chatroulette, CamSurf, Uhmegle, or Vibelly. If you prefer a service that requires accounts, which can mean fewer anonymous trolls, Emerald Chat is one option. If an adults-only space matters to you, check each service's age rules, since they differ more than you might expect.

Whichever you pick, the same safety basics apply. Never share personal details, be wary of anyone asking to move to another app, and skip and report anyone who makes you uncomfortable. Our [random video chat safety checklist](/blog/random-video-chat-safety-checklist) covers this in more detail.

If you want to try Vibelly, start with [random video chat](/random-video-chat), [text chat with strangers](/talk-to-strangers), or read how [anonymous chat](/anonymous-chat) works on Vibelly.

title: What Happened to Omegle? Why It Shut Down and What Came Next
description: Omegle went offline in November 2023 after 14 years. Why it closed, what made it popular, and what to look for in a random video chat site now.
content:
For more than a decade, Omegle was the internet's default answer to "I'm bored, let's talk to someone new." You opened the site, pressed a button, and were dropped into a conversation with a complete stranger. On November 8, 2023, that ended. The homepage was replaced by a letter from its founder, and the service never came back.

This article explains what Omegle was, why it shut down, and what the closure means for anyone looking for a random video chat site today.

## What Omegle was

Omegle launched in 2009, built by Leif K-Brooks at age 18. The idea was radically simple: no accounts, no profiles, no friend lists. You were paired with a random stranger in a text chat, identified only as "You" and "Stranger." A video mode followed in 2010, and that is the version most people remember.

The appeal was the unpredictability. You might meet a student on the other side of the world, a musician who played you a song, or someone who just wanted to talk at 3am. There was no algorithm deciding who you should see and no feed to scroll. Just one person, then the next.

## Why Omegle shut down

The same anonymity that made Omegle exciting made it very hard to run safely. With no accounts and no reliable way to know who was on the other end, the site struggled for years with misuse, including adults targeting minors and users exposing themselves on camera.

Omegle tried several measures over the years, including a separate monitored video section and automated filtering, but the problems never went away. The site also faced lawsuits, including a high-profile case in the United States brought by a woman who said she was matched with a predator through Omegle when she was a child.

In the closing letter on Omegle's homepage, K-Brooks wrote that operating Omegle was no longer sustainable, financially or psychologically, and described the constant fight against misuse as a major part of that. The message was clear: the cost of moderating an anonymous video platform at that scale had become too high.

## Why people still want random video chat

Omegle's closure did not remove the reason people used it. Millions of people still want to:

- Meet someone new without the pressure of a dating app or a social network
- Practice a language with native speakers
- Kill boredom with a conversation they could never have predicted
- Talk to someone without sharing their real identity

That demand is why a wave of alternatives appeared, and why "Omegle alternative" is still searched so often today.

## What to look for in a replacement

The lesson from Omegle is that random video chat needs real safety measures, not just a disclaimer. When you compare sites, look for:

**A clear age policy.** Random video chat with strangers is an adult activity. A good site states that it is 18+ and makes you confirm it before you start.

**A working report button.** You should be able to report someone in one tap during a call, and reports should go to people who actually act on them.

**Honest privacy claims.** Be wary of vague promises. Ask what is stored, whether calls are recorded, and how the video connection works.

**No social login just to chat.** Some services require a social media account before you can chat at all, which ties every conversation to your real identity. Asking you to sign in for specific actions, such as reporting someone, is a reasonable middle ground.

**Instant skip.** You should be able to leave any conversation immediately, without penalty.

## How Vibelly approaches it

Vibelly was built after Omegle's closure with those lessons in mind. It is strictly for adults: you confirm you are 18 or older before every chat. Every call has a Report button. Reporting requires signing in with Google or GitHub, every report is reviewed by hand, and accounts that break the community rules are banned. Video and voice calls connect directly between browsers using WebRTC, which encrypts media in transit, and calls are never recorded.

You can start a random video or text chat in your browser without installing anything. Voice-only calls and gender or country filters are available with Vibelly Premium.

No platform can make talking to strangers completely risk-free, and anyone who claims otherwise is overselling. What a platform can do is set clear rules, enforce them, and give you the tools to leave and report. That is the standard any Omegle alternative should be held to.

## The bottom line

Omegle closed because anonymous random video chat at scale is genuinely hard to run safely. The need it served is still real. If you are looking for a replacement, choose one that is upfront about being adults-only, gives you a real way to report people, and is honest about what happens to your data. Read our Safety and Community Rules page to see exactly how Vibelly handles each of these.

**Sources:** [Omegle's closing letter](https://www.omegle.com/), [Omegle on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omegle)

title: How to Stay Safe on Random Video Chat: A Practical Checklist
description: A practical safety checklist for random video chat: what never to share, how scams start, and how to handle and report bad behaviour.
content:
Random video chat can be a lot of fun. It can also put you on camera with people you know nothing about. The good news is that most risks are easy to avoid once you know what they look like. This checklist covers what to do before, during, and after a chat.

## Before you start

**Check the age policy.** Random video chat with strangers is for adults. If a site does not clearly say it is 18+, that tells you something about how it is run. On Vibelly you confirm you are 18 or older before every chat.

**Check your background.** Look at what is behind you on camera. Mail with your address, a school or work badge, a window with a recognisable view, or photos of family can all reveal more than you intend. A plain wall is the safest backdrop.

**Decide what you will share.** It is much easier to hold a line you set in advance. A good default is a first name or nickname, a country or large region, and nothing more specific.

## Never share these

- Your full name, home address, or the name of your school or workplace
- Your phone number or personal email
- Social media handles, at least until you have talked several times and feel sure
- Passwords, verification codes, or anything to do with money
- Photos or video you would not want posted publicly

Assume that anything you show on camera can be recorded by the other person. A site can refuse to record calls itself, but it cannot stop someone pointing a phone at their screen.

## How scams usually start

Most scams on random chat follow a few patterns. Recognising them is the best protection.

**"Let's move to another app."** Being pushed quickly onto a different messaging app is one of the most common warning signs. It moves you away from the site's report button and rules.

**Requests for money or gift cards.** No genuine stranger needs you to send money, buy a gift card, or "verify" anything with a payment. End the chat.

**Links to "verify" or "unlock" something.** Do not click links from strangers, especially ones that ask you to log in or enter details.

**Intimate requests.** Requests to undress or perform on camera can lead to sextortion, where the other person records you and then demands money. If this happens, do not pay, stop responding, keep any evidence, and report it.

## During the chat

**Trust your instincts.** If a conversation feels off, it probably is. You do not owe a stranger an explanation.

**Use skip freely.** Skipping is not rude. It is what the button is for. On Vibelly you can move to the next person at any time.

**Report bad behaviour.** If someone breaks the rules, report them before you skip. On Vibelly every call has a Report button. Reporting requires you to be signed in, which stops the button being abused, and every report is reviewed by hand, with bans for accounts that break the community rules.

**Keep it in the chat.** Conversations that stay on the platform stay under its rules. Be cautious about moving anywhere else.

## After the chat

**Do not follow up on pressure.** If someone found you elsewhere or keeps contacting you, block them and report them on every platform involved.

**If you were threatened or blackmailed,** do not pay. Save screenshots, usernames, and times, report the account, and contact your local police. Paying almost never makes it stop.

**Talk to someone.** If a chat upset you, it is worth telling a friend. Bad experiences feel smaller when you are not carrying them alone.

## A quick checklist

- The site is clearly 18+ and you are too
- Your background reveals nothing personal
- You share only a first name and a general location
- You never send money, codes, or intimate content
- You stay on the platform and ignore "move to another app" requests
- You skip anything that feels wrong and report rule-breakers

Random video chat works best when it is light, curious, and on your terms. Set your limits before you start, and do not be afraid to press skip. For the full rules on Vibelly, read our Safety and Community Rules page.

title: How to Choose an Omegle Alternative: 7 Things That Actually Matter
description: Seven practical checks for comparing Omegle alternatives: age policy, reporting, social login, privacy, cost, browser support, and feel.
content:
Since Omegle shut down in November 2023, dozens of sites have called themselves its replacement. Some are good. Some are thin copies full of ads and bots. A few are outright unsafe. Instead of a ranking that goes out of date in a month, here are the seven things worth checking yourself before you settle on one.

## 1. Is it clearly adults-only?

Omegle's biggest problem was minors meeting adults they should never have met. A responsible random video chat site says plainly that it is 18+ and asks you to confirm it before you chat. It is a basic step, but its absence is a red flag about everything else.

## 2. Can you report someone in one tap?

During a call you should be able to report the other person immediately, without hunting through menus. Just as important is what happens next. Look for a site that says who reviews reports and what the consequences are, such as bans for accounts that break the rules. A report button that leads nowhere is decoration.

## 3. Does it force a social media login?

Some popular services make you sign in with a social media account before you can chat. That can reduce spam, but it also ties your random conversations to your real identity. Decide how comfortable you are with that trade. If anonymity matters to you, prefer sites that let you start without linking a social account.

## 4. What does it say about privacy, specifically?

"Secure" and "private" are easy words to put on a homepage. Look for specifics:

- Are calls recorded? They should not be.
- How does the video connection work? Peer-to-peer WebRTC connections encrypt media in transit between the two browsers.
- What personal data is stored, and for how long?
- Is there a readable privacy policy?

If a site makes big claims with no explanation, treat them with caution.

## 5. What is free, and what costs money?

Most alternatives are free to start, then charge for extras. Common paid features are gender filters, country filters, and ad removal. That is a fair model, as long as the site is upfront about it. Be wary of sites where the "free" experience is so limited that you are pushed to pay within seconds.

## 6. Does it work in your browser?

You should not need to install an app just to try a random chat. A good alternative works in any modern browser on both phone and desktop, so you can test it in a minute and leave if you do not like it.

## 7. How does it feel to use?

Finally, try it. Notice how quickly you are matched, whether video quality holds up, how easy it is to skip, and whether the interface is cluttered with ads and pop-ups. Five minutes of use will tell you more than any review.

## How Vibelly measures up

We built Vibelly with this list in mind, so here is how it answers each point:

- **Adults-only:** yes. You confirm you are 18 or older before every chat.
- **Reporting:** every call has a Report button. Reports are reviewed by hand, and accounts that break the community rules are banned. Reporting requires being signed in, so it cannot be abused anonymously.
- **Login:** you can start a random chat without creating an account or linking a social media profile. Reporting, Premium, and direct messages use a Google or GitHub sign-in.
- **Privacy:** video and voice calls connect directly between browsers over WebRTC, which encrypts media in transit, and calls are never recorded.
- **Cost:** random video and text chat are free. Voice-only calls and gender and country filters are part of Vibelly Premium.
- **Browser-based:** yes, on phone and desktop, with nothing to install.

## The bottom line

The best Omegle alternative is the one that is honest with you: honest about who it is for, about what it records, and about what you have to pay for. Use the seven checks above on any site you try, including ours. If a site cannot give you clear answers, move on.

title: How to Start a Conversation With a Stranger on Video Chat
description: Opening lines, questions that work, and how to keep a conversation with a stranger going on random video chat without it feeling awkward.
content:
The first few seconds of a random video chat decide almost everything. Most people skip within moments, and usually not because the other person is unpleasant but because nothing happened. Here is how to make those first seconds count and keep a conversation going.

## Start before you say anything

People decide whether to stay before you speak. A few things help:

**Light your face.** Sit facing a window or a lamp, not with it behind you. A dark silhouette gets skipped.

**Frame yourself.** Keep your face and shoulders in the shot, with the camera roughly at eye level.

**Look approachable.** A small smile and looking at the camera, not at yourself on screen, goes a long way.

## Opening lines that work

Generic openers like "hi" or "asl" invite generic answers or an instant skip. Specific, easy-to-answer openers work better.

- "Hi! Where are you calling from?" Simple, friendly, and almost everyone answers.
- "What's the time where you are?" It is a natural follow-up to location and often leads to "why are you up so late?"
- "That's a great poster behind you, what is it?" Noticing something real in their background shows you are paying attention.
- "I'm trying to talk to someone from every continent. Where are you?" A playful mission gives the chat a purpose.
- "Quick question: what's the best thing that happened to you this week?" Upbeat and personal without being invasive.

## Questions that keep it going

Once you are past hello, open questions do the work. Questions that start with "what", "how", or "why" get longer answers than yes-or-no ones.

- "What do people where you live do on a weekend?"
- "What's something you're into that most people don't know about?"
- "How did you end up learning English?" if it is not their first language
- "What's a food from your country I have to try?"
- "What would you be doing right now if you weren't on here?"

Then follow up on what they actually say. "Wait, you play the cello? For how long?" beats moving to the next question on your list.

## Share as well as ask

A conversation where one person only asks questions feels like an interview. After they answer, offer something of your own: a small story, an opinion, a recommendation. Keep it light and do not share personal details like your full name, address, or workplace. Interesting does not mean identifiable.

## Handling awkward moments

**Silence.** A short pause is normal. Fill it with a new topic or by commenting on something you can both see.

**Language barriers.** Slow down, use simple words, and do not be afraid to type a word in the chat box. Many great conversations happen in a mix of two languages.

**They are not interested.** Some people want something different from you, and that is fine. Say "nice talking to you" and skip. No hard feelings.

**They cross a line.** If someone is rude, sexual, or pushy, you do not need to be polite about it. Skip, and report them if they broke the rules. On Vibelly every call has a Report button for signed-in users.

## Ending well

Good conversations end too. A simple "This was really fun, good luck with your exam!" leaves both of you with a good memory. If you would genuinely like to talk again, be careful about swapping social handles with someone you just met. Take your time and trust your instincts.

## Try it

The best way to get better at talking to strangers is practice, and random video chat gives you lots of it with nothing on the line. On Vibelly you can start a free video or text chat in your browser in a few seconds. Vibelly is for adults 18+.

title: How to Practice a Language With Native Speakers on Random Video Chat
description: Random video chat is an underrated way to practice speaking a new language. How to find native speakers, what to say, and how to improve.
content:
Apps can teach you vocabulary and grammar, but they cannot make you comfortable speaking to a real person in real time. That is the skill most learners struggle with, and it only improves with practice. Random video chat is a surprisingly good place to get it.

## Why random chat works for speaking practice

**Real, unscripted conversation.** Textbook dialogues are tidy. Real speakers talk fast, use slang, and change topic. Random chat exposes you to all of it.

**Low stakes.** If a conversation goes badly, you skip and start again. Nobody you know is watching, which makes it easier to take risks and make mistakes.

**Volume.** Progress comes from lots of short conversations. Random chat lets you have several in the time it takes to schedule a single lesson.

**Accents and variety.** You will hear the same language spoken in different countries and regions, which trains your ear far better than a single teacher.

## Finding native speakers

On a global random chat you will meet people from many countries, so you will not always land on a speaker of your target language. A few ways to improve the odds:

- **Use a country filter if you have one.** On Vibelly, country filters are part of Vibelly Premium and let you match with people in a specific country.
- **Pick your timing.** Chat during evening hours in the countries where your target language is spoken.
- **Ask directly.** "Do you speak Spanish? I'm learning and would love to practice" is a perfectly good opener. Many people are happy to help.
- **Offer a trade.** Suggest splitting the time: ten minutes in their language, ten in yours. People are more generous when they get practice too.

## What to say

Prepare a few simple topics so you are not searching for words under pressure:

- Introductions: your name, where you are from, why you are learning
- Daily life: work or study, food, weekends, the weather
- Their country: favourite places, local food, what you should visit
- Opinions: music, films, and series you both know

Write down five or six questions in your target language before you start. Having them ready removes most of the panic.

## Turn chats into progress

Short conversations only become progress if you learn from them.

**Keep a notebook open.** Write down new words and phrases as you hear them, and look them up after the chat.

**Ask to be corrected.** Say early on, "Please correct me if I say something wrong." Most people will not interrupt you otherwise.

**Repeat topics.** Having the same "where are you from" conversation ten times is not boring for learning. Each time you get faster and more natural.

**Set a small goal.** For example, three conversations in your target language per session. Small, consistent goals beat occasional marathons.

## Stay safe while you practice

Language practice is a great reason to chat, but the usual rules still apply. Share only your first name and a general location, never send money or personal details, and be cautious about moving the conversation to another app. If anyone makes you uncomfortable, skip and report them. Our safety checklist covers this in more detail.

## Get started

Pick your five starter questions, open a chat, and say hello in the language you are learning. The first conversation is the hardest. By the tenth, you will notice the difference. On Vibelly you can start a free random video or text chat in your browser in seconds. Vibelly is for adults 18+.
